questions.q: What does LePera identify as the root of unexplained anxiety and burnout?
a: An impaired connection between mind, body and spirit
A shortage of vitamins in the diet
A genetic condition with no treatment
Too much time spent at work
questions.why: The overview says these symptoms come from a damaged mind-body-spirit connection rather than a medical problem.

questions.q: How does LePera say childhood trauma can be healed?
a: Revisit the old wounds and learn healthier ways to cope
Ignore the memories until they fade
Replace them with positive affirmations
Talk only about the present, never the past
questions.why: Lesson one says healing means feeling the old emotions again and replacing childhood defenses with honest expression.

questions.q: What happens to the amygdala after trauma, according to the summary?
a: It stays on alert and sees threats everywhere
It shrinks and stops responding to danger
It becomes focused only on pleasant memories
It transfers its duties to the cortex
questions.why: Lesson two says trauma makes the fear center misfire, so the body remains in constant alert mode.

questions.q: Which practice does LePera recommend for calming the body's threat response?
a: Mindful breathing, along with better sleep and diet
High-intensity exercise every morning
Long periods of fasting each week
Keeping a detailed dream journal
questions.why: Lesson two recommends breathing exercises, more sleep and healthier food to disarm the survival system.

questions.q: What three types of boundaries does LePera describe?
a: Physical, resource and emotional
Social, financial and spiritual
Personal, professional and digital
Emotional, mental and physical
questions.why: Lesson three walks through physical limits, boundaries around time and money, and emotional boundaries.
